description: Lines up 2 to 5 U.S.-listed stocks or ETFs side by side on Market Eyes Live MELANY ratings: conviction tier (weakest to strongest: Unfavorable, Hold, Favorable, Highest Conviction), 0 to 100 composite score, and the valuation, quality and momentum factor scores. Use this when the user wants several tickers' ratings shown together, for example 'compare AAPL, MSFT and GOOGL on quality and valuation' or 'NVDA vs AMD ratings'. Do not use for real-time quotes, price history, options, crypto, futures, non-U.S. listings, or a personal recommendation. Limitations: draws only on the daily-refreshed rated set; a ticker outside it returns a note instead of scores (get_stock_rating can score a covered ticker live), and a ticker outside U.S.-listed stocks and ETFs returns a not-covered note; it does not return entry zones, alert levels or position sizing (has_trade_plan marks a ticker for which Market Eyes Live has a trade plan; the plan values are part of a Market Eyes Live subscription). Methodology and the graded public record: https://marketeyeslive.com/how-melany-is-tested.html. Research data, not financial advice; this tool is read-only and never places trades.
name: compare_stocks

comparison.description: one row per distinct requested ticker, in input order (BRK.B and BRK-B are one ticker)

has_trade_plan.description: present (true) only when Market Eyes Live has a trade plan for this ticker; the plan values are not included

note.description: present instead of scores: the ticker is outside the daily-refreshed set, not on the coverage list, not covered, or shares its symbol with a futures contract or coin

rating_tier.description: Conviction tier. Mature ladder, weakest to strongest: Unfavorable, Hold, Favorable, Highest Conviction. Favorable and Highest Conviction are both favorable reads; Highest Conviction is a composite of 69 or above (for a stock, a small hysteresis can hold a borderline label steady between refreshes; a fund or REIT word follows its label in the app, which has none). Names the mature ladder does not cover carry their own label: Promising, then Very Promising, then Rising Star for names without mature fundamentals, Runner! for a momentum surge, Catalyst Watch for a news-driven gap up on volume. ETFs and REITs use the same mature ladder, chosen by the tone of the fund's own label in the app (a favorable fund label reads Favorable or Highest Conviction, a cautious or neutral one Hold, a negative one Unfavorable); a leveraged or inverse fund never reads above Hold. These nine words are the complete set; null when no tier applies.
